title_en: Regulations on the Work of Specially Invited Consultants of the Supreme People's Court
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Regulations on Special Advisory Counselors

Fa Fa [1999] No. 13

Article 1 These Regulations are formulated to strengthen and improve the adjudicative work of the people's courts, ensure the correct implementation of laws, and uphold judicial impartiality.

Article 2 Special Advisory Counselors of the Supreme People's Court are persons appointed by the Supreme People's Court to provide consultations and offer suggestions on the adjudicative work and team building of the people's courts.

Article 3 Special Advisory Counselors of the Supreme People's Court shall be composed of renowned legal scholars and prominent figures.

Special Advisory Counselors are appointed by the Supreme People's Court, with a term of office of three years per session.

Article 4 Duties of Special Advisory Counselors:

(1) To provide advisory opinions on the implementation of the Party's line, principles, and policies, and on the implementation of major work deployments of the Party Central Committee and the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress by the people's courts.

(2) To offer suggestions on the fair adjudication of cases and enforcement work by the people's courts in accordance with the law.

(3) To provide advisory opinions on matters such as team building, adjudication of significant and difficult cases, and the drafting of judicial interpretations by the people's courts.

(4) To reflect or transmit opinions from the public concerning instances where the people's courts or their adjudicators fail to handle cases according to law in judicial activities, thereby affecting judicial impartiality.

Article 5 Special Advisory Counselors, in carrying out their work, shall seek truth from facts, be objective and fair, not seek personal gain, not engage in favoritism, conscientiously abide by the laws and regulations of the state, and strictly observe the state confidentiality system.

Article 6 Special Advisory Counselors may, based on actual circumstances, hold symposiums on a regular or irregular basis to carry out their work, or may provide advisory opinions on a particular matter at any time.

Article 7 The relevant people's courts shall earnestly handle the suggestions and improvement opinions raised by Special Advisory Counselors, and provide feedback on the handling status and results to the Special Advisory Counselor who made the suggestion or improvement opinion.

Article 8 Local people's courts at various levels and special people's courts shall provide support, cooperation, and facilitation for the work of Special Advisory Counselors.

Article 9 The Supreme People's Court shall establish an Office of Special Advisory Counselors, responsible for daily administrative affairs.

Article 10 These Regulations shall be effective as of the date of promulgation.

May 12, 1999
